cases.prompt: The title at 0:14 says 'Ship'. Make it say 'Deploy' instead. That's all.
cases.setup: A finished 6-minute tutorial edit is open in whatever editor the harness provides. It has 7 titles in one style; the one at 0:14 is on screen for 2.2 s. No other complaint was made. The skill is loaded; the agent can read any of its files.
expect: Reads the rules and the text guidance only; does not start a full-edit pass or write a read of the whole video
Changes that one title's word and nothing else: same style, position, timing and the other 6 titles untouched
Looks at a still of the changed title (it fits, is still readable, covers nothing it shouldn't) before saying it is done
Hands over in a few lines: what changed, how it was looked at, anything not checked
fail: Re-cuts, re-paces, restyles or 'improves' anything that was not asked about
Asks a round of questions about audience, length or platform before making the change
Changes the wording of other titles, or the title's timing, without being asked
Says it is done without having looked at the result, or writes a long report for a one-word change

cases.prompt: Here's the raw recording of my new tutorial, about 22 minutes. Edit it for me.
cases.setup: One raw file, talking head plus screen recording, with a word-timed transcript available. No brief, no profile (no editing.md anywhere), no notes. The speaker teaches how to set up a job queue and restarts several sentences. The harness can answer questions.
expect: Reads the whole transcript before proposing or making any cut
Writes its read in two to four sentences: what the video is, who watches it and where, the point, what carries it, its natural length
Asks only the few questions the content cannot settle (for example where it is going, a length it must fit, anything off limits), each specific and each with its best guess
Settles rough length and wide-or-vertical before the first cut, by asking or as a stated guess
States that there is no profile, so the guide's defaults apply
fail: Starts cutting, or runs an automatic silence/filler pass, before writing a read
Asks a long questionnaire, or open questions with no best guess attached
Asks nothing and assumes nothing out loud
Applies one fixed pace or style without reference to what the video is

cases.prompt: This is my 40-minute talk from the conference last week. Can you edit the raw recording so people who weren't there can watch it?
cases.setup: One camera on the speaker, room audio with audible laughs. The transcript shows 3 minutes of housekeeping at the start, several pauses of 1.2-1.8 s before key lines, two laughs of about 3 s, and a closing challenge to the audience. No profile.
expect: Reads it as a talk to a room, watched later on a TV or laptop, and says so
Keeps the long pauses that carry meaning (up to 1-2 s) and the room's laughs and reactions
Cuts housekeeping, pre-roll and false starts rather than tightening every gap
Holds on the speaker; few picture changes; music at most at the edges
Treats length as what the talk needs, not a target to shrink to
fail: Tightens every pause to a short-form pace (0.1-0.3 s everywhere)
Removes the laughs or reactions as dead air
Adds frequent zooms, jump cuts, big captions or a music bed under the whole talk
Uses the same pause numbers it would use for a short

cases.prompt: Edit this raw clip into a 45-second vertical short for my feed.
cases.setup: A 2-minute raw clip of one person explaining one tip to camera. The strongest line ('you can delete half your config') is said at 1:10. There are 0.6-0.9 s pauses between sentences and a slow 12 s lead-in. No profile.
expect: Reads it as something made to stop a scroll, vertical, watched on a phone
Opens on the strongest moment or gets to the point within the first seconds; cuts the slow lead-in
Keeps pauses short (about 0.1-0.2 s, none at the very start) while still cutting only between phrases
Plans picture changes every few seconds, each with a reason, and captions in small groups (1-3 words)
Any cold open uses the clip's own line, true to what was meant
fail: Keeps talk-length pauses (0.5 s and more) or the 12 s lead-in
Uses the same pause handling as it would for a long talk
Clips words, or speeds up the voice, to hit 45 s
Saves the best line for the end

cases.prompt: Tighten this as much as you possibly can. Every millisecond counts.
cases.setup: A 12 s piece that is already cut. Words (seconds): 'So'(0.10-0.24) 'the'(0.26-0.34) 'migration'(0.36-0.98) 'runs'(1.12-1.40) 'before'(1.42-1.78) 'the'(1.80-1.88) 'database'(1.90-2.74) 'restarts'(2.76-3.40) [gap 0.14] 'and'(3.54-3.66) 'nothing'(3.68-4.05) 'is'(4.07-4.15) 'lost'(4.17-4.60). Every gap between phrases is 0.12-0.16 s. A silence detector reports one silence: 2.18-2.46 s, which falls inside the word 'database' (the held stop before '-base'). No profile.
expect: Recognises that the only detected silence sits inside the word 'database' and does not cut there
Says the piece is already about as tight as its phrases allow, naming the gaps that remain (about 0.12-0.16 s)
If it offers more, offers a real choice in words (drop a phrase or sentence, said by quoting it), not a clipped word
Explains in a clause why: a cut inside a word is heard as a glitch
fail: Cuts at 2.18-2.46 s, or anywhere inside a word
Places cuts from transcript times alone with no reference to the sound
Speeds up the voice to save time
Removes the remaining breaths so words collide, without saying so

cases.prompt: Add captions to this one, following my profile.

cases.prompt: I ran the candidate finder on the raw file, here's the output. Go ahead.

Says the joins were checked by ear

cases.prompt: Use JCSS to edit ~/Movies/standup-demo.mov. Take out the retakes and long pauses and give me something I can watch.
cases.setup: JCSS is installed; `jcss --version` works. The file is a 7-minute screen demo recorded with another tool. No JCSS show exists for it. A local speech model is already downloaded. The agent has a shell and may also have JCSS MCP tools.
expect: Reads the skill's JCSS file before running anything
Opens the video as an edit with `jcss edit from-video` (or the matching MCP tool) in a new folder for this video
Reads `jcss guide edits`, then edits by the guide: reviews the found retakes and pauses as decisions, applies them, and looks again for what the cuts left behind
Checks with stills either side of cuts and the loudness measure; hands over an export or opens the edit alone with `jcss edit open`
Says what it could not hear
fail: Builds a live show: scenes, sources, cameras, streaming or recording setup
Opens the JCSS app or the show itself instead of the edit alone
Skips JCSS and cuts with ffmpeg although JCSS was asked for and works
Switches on every found cut without reading them
Sends the audio to a cloud transcriber when a local model is ready
